preamble: Replacement of the voiceless alveolar lateral fricative [ɬ] by the plain lateral approximant [l] (loss of frication plus voicing). The documented cases are loanword adaptations into languages without [ɬ]: English renders Welsh ll [ɬ] and Tibetan lh [ɬ] as [l] (Lloyd, Llandudno, Lhasa), and Mandarin does the same in Tibetan place names (拉孜 Lāzī from lha rtse, 洛扎 Luòzhā from lho brag). No inherited diachronic ɬ > l change has been identified. Welsh soft mutation ll → l is a morphological alternation and is not counted here.

examples.note: Surname borrowed from Welsh; the lateral fricative is replaced by English [l].
Given name borrowed from Welsh with [ɬ] rendered as [l].
Place name borrowed with initial [ɬ] rendered as [l].
Tibetan ལྷ lh- [ɬ] is rendered as English [l].
Tibetan [ɬ] is replaced by Mandarin [l], which has no lateral fricative.
